mainTopic: Witnesses who weaken their own document (אמנה, מודעא, condition), keeping an עולה at home, and outsiders who confirm dead signers' handwriting
overview: The amud opens with רב ששת בריה דרב אידי, who learns from רב כהנא that witnesses who say their document was only a שטר אמנה are not believed, because witnesses would not sign an עולה. The פסוק 'ואל תשכן באהליך עולה' then teaches that one may not keep a שטר פרוע, a שטר אמנה, or an unproofread ספר at home. רב נחמן rules that witnesses who claim אמנה or מודעא are not believed. מר בר רב אשי says a מודעא claim is believed, since such a document may be written. רב נחמן tells רבא that witnesses who mention a condition are believed: the parties must fulfill the condition first. When only one witness mentions a condition, רב פפא says one cannot outweigh two. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagrees and says that witness undoes his own testimony, and the הלכה follows him. Finally, a ברייתא about outsiders who identify dead signers' handwriting raises a 'two against two' question, and רב ששת begins answering that a הכחשה is the start of a הזמה. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Witnesses who claim the document was only a trust document are not believed
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי learns from רב כהנא that witnesses who say 'our document was a שטר אמנה' are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת son of רב אידי said: From רב כהנא's statement we can learn that if witnesses say 'the document we signed was only a trust document,' they are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי draws a practical rule out of an earlier statement of רב כהנא. Witnesses who later say the loan document they signed was fake, only a 'trust' document, are not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר אמנה is a loan document written before any money was actually lent, based on trust that the loan will happen. If witnesses signed such a document and now try to undo it by calling it a שטר אמנה, their claim is rejected. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'trust' document: a loan document written although no money was actually given yet
'Learn from it': we can draw a conclusion from this

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi said:
Learn from Rav Kahana's statement:
witnesses who said, "Our words were a matter of trust"
phrases.notes: Meaning: 'the document we signed was only a trust document, and no real loan took place.'

phrases.english: are not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new rule from the earlier statement of רב כהנא that came before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who claim their signed document was only a שטר אמנה are not believed.

steps.title: Why are they not believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why these witnesses are not believed. This short question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the same witnesses who give a document its strength can also explain it. So the גמרא wants to know why their explanation is rejected here.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why witnesses who claim the document was a שטר אמנה are not believed.

steps.title: Honest witnesses do not sign something false
steps.stepSummary: A שטר אמנה is an injustice, and witnesses would not sign an injustice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since such a document is an injustice, witnesses would not sign on an injustice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a שטר אמנה is a wrongful, false document. We assume kosher witnesses would never sign one, so their claim is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'it was a שטר אמנה,' the witnesses are really admitting they signed something false. We do not accept a claim that makes them wrongdoers. We assume they signed a true document.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses who say 'the document was only a שטר אמנה' are not believed, because signing such a document is an עולה, and we assume witnesses do not sign an עולה.

phrases.english: Since it is an injustice,
they would not sign on an injustice.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּעַוְלָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שטר אמנה is an עולה, and witnesses are presumed not to sign an עולה, so their claim is rejected.

steps.title: Do not keep a paid-up loan document at home
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids keeping a שטר פרוע at home, based on 'ואל תשכן באהליך עולה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A person may not keep a paid-up loan document in his house, because the verse says, 'Let not injustice dwell in your tents.'
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the idea of a document being an 'עולה,' the גמרא brings רבי יהושע בן לוי. He says a person may not keep a loan document that was already paid off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a loan is paid, the document is false: it still claims a debt that no longer exists. Keeping it at home is like letting an עולה live in your tent, because someone could use it to collect again. The פסוק from איוב is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document that was already paid off
To keep, to leave lying around
'Let not injustice dwell in your tents' (איוב 11:14)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the source for the general rule that one should not keep things at home that could lead to wrongdoing. The rest of this section builds on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
It is forbidden for a person
to keep a paid-up loan document in his house,
because it is said:
"Let not injustice dwell in your tents."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: אָסוּר לוֹ לָאָדָם שֶׁיְּשַׁהֶה שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the word עולה in step 3 to a related rule about keeping false documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to keep a שטר פרוע in one's house, because of 'ואל תשכן באהליך עולה'.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל, רב's reading of both halves of the verse
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב: the first half of the פסוק is about a שטר אמנה and a שטר פסים; the second half is about a שטר פרוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they said in רב's name: 'If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away' refers to a trust document and a security document. 'And let not injustice dwell in your tents' refers to a paid-up document.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל bring a teaching of רב that reads the whole פסוק in איוב 11:14. He splits it into two halves, each about a different kind of document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'און בידך' (iniquity in your hand) is applied to a שטר אמנה and a שטר פסים, documents that were false from the start. 'עולה באהליך' (injustice in your tents) is applied to a שטר פרוע, a document that became false once the loan was paid. Both kinds must not be kept.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away': the first half of the same פסוק
A 'פסים' document, translated here as a security document; another kind of document that may not be kept

phrases.english: In the West they say in Rav's name:
"If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away":
phrases.notes: איוב 11:14, the first half of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: this is a trust document and a security document.
"And let not injustice dwell in your tents":
this is a paid-up document.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fuller reading of the same פסוק used in step 4, covering more kinds of documents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first half of איוב 11:14 forbids keeping a שטר אמנה and a שטר פסים; the second half forbids keeping a שטר פרוע.

steps.title: Comparing the opinions: paid-up documents versus trust documents
steps.stepSummary: Whoever forbids a שטר פרוע surely forbids a שטר אמנה. But whoever forbids a שטר אמנה might allow keeping a שטר פרוע, since it is sometimes held for the scribe's fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said a paid-up document is forbidden would certainly forbid a trust document. But the one who said a trust document is forbidden might permit a paid-up document, because sometimes it is kept back until the scribe's fee is paid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the opinions about which document the word 'עולה' refers to. It shows how far each opinion reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר אמנה was false from day one, so it is worse than a שטר פרוע, which was once true. That is why forbidding the שטר פרוע automatically forbids the שטר אמנה (a כל שכן). The reverse does not follow: a lender sometimes has a fair reason to hold a paid-up document, as security for the scribe's fee that the borrower still owes.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says, the opinion that holds
The scribe's coins: the fee for writing the document

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the second opinion as saying a שטר פרוע is a fine document. It only explains why keeping one for a while can be justified, because the lender may be holding it until the scribe is paid.
steps.whatToRemember: A שטר אמנה (false from the start) is worse than a שטר פרוע (once true). Forbidding the weaker case covers the stronger one, but not the other way around.

phrases.english: The one who said a paid-up document is forbidden,
all the more so a trust document.
And the one who said a trust document is forbidden,
but a paid-up document, not,
because sometimes one holds on to it
for the scribe's coins.
phrases.notes: The borrower pays the scribe who wrote the document, so the lender may keep it until that fee is covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן שְׁטַר אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes how far the opinions in steps 4 and 5 reach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Forbidding a שטר פרוע includes a שטר אמנה by כל שכן. Forbidding only a שטר אמנה need not include a שטר פרוע, since it may be held legitimately for the scribe's fee.

steps.title: An unproofread ספר may be kept only thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי: an unproofread ספר may be kept for up to thirty days; after that it is forbidden, because of 'ואל תשכן באהליך עולה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: About a book that has not been proofread, רבי אמי said: Up to thirty days it is permitted to keep it; from then on it is forbidden to keep it, because the verse says, 'Let not injustice dwell in your tents.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling built on the same פסוק. רבי אמי says a ספר that was not checked for mistakes may be kept uncorrected for only thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספר with mistakes in it is also a kind of 'עולה' in the house, since people may learn wrong things from it. רבי אמי gives thirty days to fix it. After that, keeping it uncorrected is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated': introduces a teaching of the אמוראים
A book (ספר) that has not been proofread and corrected
From here onward, after this point

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the פסוק of 'עולה' reaches past loan documents to anything in the home that could lead people into error.

phrases.english: It was stated:
A book that is not proofread,
Rabbi Ami said:
up to thirty days it is permitted to keep it,
from then on it is forbidden to keep it,
because it is said:
"Let not injustice dwell in your tents."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: סֵפֶר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּגָּהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same פסוק from steps 4 and 5 to a new case: an unproofread ספר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unproofread ספר may be kept up to thirty days; after that, keeping it is forbidden because of 'ואל תשכן באהליך עולה'.

steps.title: Witnesses who claim trust or a hidden protest are not believed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that witnesses who say the שטר was really an אמנה, or that a מודעא went along with it, are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Witnesses who say, 'Our signing was only a trust arrangement,' are not believed. If they say, 'Our signing came with a protest declaration,' they are also not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב נחמן says witnesses who signed a שטר cannot later weaken it by saying it was an אמנה or that there was a מודעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמנה means no real loan took place; the document was written on trust. A מודעא means the signer had privately declared he was being forced. In both cases רב נחמן does not let the witnesses undercut the document they signed.

keyTerms.meaning: Trust: a document written before any real loan took place
A private declaration that one is being forced into a deal, which cancels it
Our words, meaning our testimony or our signing

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Witnesses who said
"Our words were a matter of trust"
phrases.notes: They admit they signed, but say no real loan happened yet. It was written on trust.

phrases.english: are not believed.
"Our words came with a declaration of protest"
are not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: עֵדִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֲמָנָה הָיוּ דְּבָרֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about witnesses weakening a שטר, after the topic of keeping wrong documents at home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who claim אמנה or מודעא are not believed.

steps.title: A second view splits the two cases
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי agrees about אמנה but holds that witnesses claiming מודעא are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: If they say 'it was trust,' they are not believed. If they say 'there was a protest declaration,' they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי disagrees with רב נחמן on one of the two cases. He treats a מודעא claim differently from an אמנה claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that witnesses are not believed about אמנה. The argument is only about מודעא, where מר בר רב אשי accepts the witnesses' claim.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the son of רב אשי

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
"Our words were trust": they are not believed;
"Our words came with a protest declaration": they are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן about the מודעא case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses are believed about מודעא, but not about אמנה.

steps.title: Why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why מר בר רב אשי treats the two cases differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind מר בר רב אשי's split. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both claims seem to weaken the document in the same way. So the גמרא wants to know what separates them.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is a מודעא claim believed but an אמנה claim not?

steps.title: One document may be written, the other may not
steps.stepSummary: A document with a מודעא is allowed to be written, but an אמנה document is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the מודעא document) is allowed to be written. That one (the אמנה document) is not allowed to be written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that witnesses may properly sign a document that has a מודעא, but they may not sign an אמנה document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'there was a מודעא' does not admit to any wrongdoing, so the witnesses can be believed. Saying 'it was an אמנה' would mean they signed something forbidden. Step 3 already said witnesses would not sign an injustice, so this claim is rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: According to מר בר רב אשי, the test is whether the witnesses were allowed to sign such a document. A מודעא document is allowed; an אמנה document is not.

phrases.english: This one may be written.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the document that came with a מודעא.

phrases.english: And this one may not be written.
phrases.notes: This is the אמנה document, which is a wrong done to the borrower.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נִיתַּן לִיכָּתֵב וְהַאי לֹא נִיתַּן לִיכָּתֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מודעא document may be written, but an אמנה document is forbidden, so witnesses would not admit to signing one.

steps.title: What if the witnesses say there was a condition?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether witnesses who say the deal had a condition are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: If witnesses say, 'Our signing was based on a condition,' what is the law? Maybe it is like מודעא and אמנה, which are rejected because they uproot the document, and this also uproots the document. Or maybe a condition is a different matter?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new case to רב נחמן: witnesses confirm their signatures but say the deal depended on a condition. He lays out the two possible ways to look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On one side, a condition seems to undo the document, just like אמנה and מודעא. On the other side, a condition does not deny that the document is real. It only adds something that still has to happen.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition attached to the deal

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
"Our words were conditional": what is the law?
With a protest declaration and trust, this is the reason:
because they uproot the document;
and this one also uproots the document.
Or perhaps:
a condition is a different matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן: תְּנַאי הָיוּ דְּבָרֵינוּ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב נחמן's ruling in step 8 and asks about a new kind of claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a claim of a condition treated like אמנה and מודעא (rejected), or is it different?

steps.title: Go fulfill your condition first
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the court tells the parties to fulfill the condition and then come back for judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When they come before us for judgment, we tell them: Go fulfill your conditions, and then come down for judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules that the witnesses are believed about the condition. The document cannot be collected until the condition is fulfilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition is different from אמנה and מודעא. It does not cancel the document; it only delays it. So the witnesses' added statement is accepted, and the document goes into effect once the condition is fulfilled.
steps.whatToRemember: A claim of a condition is believed. The document is enforced only after the condition is fulfilled.

phrases.english: He said to him:
When they come before us for judgment,
we say to them:
Go fulfill your conditions
and then come down for judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי אָתוּ לְקַמַּן לְדִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A condition is a different matter. The witnesses are believed, and the condition must be fulfilled before the document is enforced.

steps.title: One witness says there was a condition, the other says there was none
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the case where the two witnesses disagree about whether there was a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says, 'There was a condition,' and the other witness says, 'There was no condition.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new case where the witnesses split on the condition. This sets up רב פפא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both witnesses agree they signed. They disagree only about the condition. So the question is whether one witness's mention of a condition is enough to hold up the document.

phrases.english: One witness says "There was a condition,"
and one witness says "There was no condition."

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אוֹמֵר תְּנַאי וְעֵד אוֹמֵר אֵינוֹ תְּנַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the condition case of step 13 to a split between the witnesses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the document valid when only one witness mentions a condition?

steps.title: One witness cannot outweigh two
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that the document is valid, since both witnesses confirm it and only one mentions a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Both of them testify about a good, valid document. The one who says 'there was a condition' is only one witness, and the words of one do not count against two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא says the document stands. Two witnesses back the valid document, and only one raises the condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא splits each witness's testimony into two parts: 'this is a valid document' and 'there was a condition.' Both witnesses said the first part, but only one said the second. A single witness cannot overturn the testimony of two.

keyTerms.term: אֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: The words of one witness do not count against two

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Both of them testify about a valid document,
and this one who says "There was a condition"
is just one,
and the words of one
do not count where there are two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בִּשְׁטָרָא מְעַלְּיָא קָא מַסְהֲדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the case raised in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The document is valid, because one witness cannot outweigh two.

steps.title: Then even two witnesses saying condition should not count
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע argues that רב פפא's logic would also reject a condition when both witnesses mention it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע objected: If so, then even when both of them say there was a condition, it should also not count?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע attacks רב פפא's reasoning. He shows that it would lead to a result that goes against רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If confirming the signature counts as separate testimony that the document is valid, then even two witnesses who mention a condition would be contradicting what they already said. But רב נחמן ruled in step 13 that two witnesses are believed about a condition. So רב פפא's logic must be wrong.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua objected:
If so,
then even when both of them say it, too?
phrases.notes: He means: by רב פפא's logic, even two witnesses saying 'condition' should be ignored, but רב נחמן said they are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's reasoning in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's idea that confirming the signature is separate testimony about a valid document
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That idea would also reject a condition mentioned by both witnesses, which goes against רב נחמן's ruling.

steps.title: Mentioning a condition undoes your own testimony
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that a witness who mentions a condition is pulling back his own testimony, so only one witness is left supporting the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we say: These two come to uproot their own testimony. So this single one also comes to uproot his own testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his own way of looking at the case. A witness who mentions a condition is weakening what he himself testified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both witnesses mention a condition, their statement takes back their own testimony that the document is valid, and we accept that. In the same way, a single witness who mentions a condition takes back his own support. That leaves only one witness backing the document, which is not enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think of רב פפא's case as one witness against two. For רב הונא, the witness who says 'condition' takes away his own support, so only one witness is left backing the document.

phrases.english: Rather, we say:
these two come to uproot their own testimony;
this one also comes to uproot his own testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמְרִינַן: הָנֵי לְמִיעְקַר סָהֲדוּתַיְיהוּ קָאָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers רב הונא's reasoning in place of רב פפא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who mentions a condition undoes his own testimony, so the document has only one witness supporting it.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רב הונא the son of רב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument in favor of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one witness who says there was a condition is believed about his own testimony. So the document cannot simply be collected on the strength of the other witness alone.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. A witness who mentions a condition takes back his own support, so even one such witness weakens the document.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides in practice how a court treats a document when the witnesses disagree about a condition.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: And the halakha is like Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between רב פפא and רב הונא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: a single witness who mentions a condition undoes his own testimony.

steps.title: Witnesses who confirm the handwriting can also cancel the document
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that two people who identify dead signers' handwriting are believed when they add that the signers were forced, minors, or unfit witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Two witnesses signed a document and then died. Two people from the street came and said, 'We know this is their handwriting, but they were forced, or they were minors, or they were unfit witnesses.' These two are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a שטר whose signers have died. Two outside people identify the signatures but say the signing was not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without these two people, nobody could confirm the signatures, so the שטר would have no strength at all. Since the same people who make the שטר usable are the ones who cancel it, we believe them on both parts. This is the idea of הפה שאסר הוא הפה שהתיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
A legal document, such as a loan document
People who are not allowed to serve as witnesses

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Two witnesses signed on a document and they died,
and two people came from the marketplace and said:
We know that it is their handwriting,
but they were forced,
they were minors,
they were disqualified witnesses —
these are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the ruling like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside witnesses who confirm the signatures are believed when they say the signing was invalid.

steps.title: When the handwriting is already confirmed, they are not believed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the signatures are confirmed by other witnesses or by a document that בית דין upheld, the two outsiders are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if other witnesses say this is their handwriting, or their handwriting can be matched to another document that was challenged and upheld in court, these two are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side of its rule. Once the signatures are proven without these two people, their claim that the signing was invalid is no longer accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason they were believed before was that the שטר depended only on them. Here the שטר stands on its own proof, so their word that the signers were unfit is not enough to cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge to a document's validity
Was confirmed as valid in court

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second case is a different kind of document. It is the same שטר. The only change is that the signatures are proven by someone else, so the two outsiders are no longer the only basis for the שטר.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁכְּתַב יָדָם הוּא זֶה,
phrases.english: But if there are other witnesses that this is their handwriting,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה כְּתַב יָדָם יוֹצֵא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר
phrases.english: or their handwriting comes out from another place,
from a document that someone challenged
phrases.notes: Their signatures on this other document can be compared to the signatures on our שטר.

phrases.english: and it was confirmed in court —
these are not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁכְּתַב יָדָם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, giving the case where the outsiders are not believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the signatures are proven without the two outsiders, their claim that the signing was invalid is not accepted.

steps.title: Why can the document collect? It is two against two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the שטר can be fully valid for collecting when the two signers stand against the two outsiders.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we really collect with it like a good document? Why? It is two witnesses against two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the end of the ברייתא. Even if the outsiders are not believed, why should the שטר be fully valid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two signers, through their confirmed signatures, say the loan is valid. The two outsiders say the signing was invalid. When two witnesses contradict two, the usual result is doubt, so the שטר should not be able to take money.

phrases.english: And do we collect with it as with a fully valid document?
But why?
It is two against two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַגְבֵּינַן בֵּיהּ כְּבִשְׁטָרָא מְעַלְּיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of step 20 that the שטר is fully valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied ruling that the שטר collects like a fully valid document when the outsiders are not believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two against two creates a doubt, and a doubtful שטר should not be able to take money.

steps.title: רב ששת: contradiction is the start of הזמה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת learns from the ברייתא that a הכחשה is the beginning of a הזמה. His full point continues after this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This teaches that contradicting witnesses is the beginning of proving them false.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת begins to answer the 'two against two' question. He says the ברייתא shows that a הכחשה is the first stage of a הזמה. His full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a הכחשה just leaves us in doubt, while a הזמה fully defeats the witnesses. רב ששת says the ברייתא treats a הכחשה as partly like a הזמה. The details of how this solves the question come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches; a rule learned from the source just quoted
Contradiction: witnesses say the event did not happen as described
Proving witnesses false by showing they were somewhere else at the time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הכחשה and הזמה. A הכחשה argues about what happened. A הזמה attacks the witnesses themselves by placing them elsewhere. רב ששת says the first is the start of the second, not that they are the same.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: This is to say:
contradiction is the beginning of הזמה,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the 'two against two' challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learns a new rule from the ברייתא about the strength of a הכחשה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two against two is a plain doubt, so the שטר should not be able to collect.
steps.terutzMaskana: A הכחשה is the beginning of a הזמה. The full answer continues on the next amud.
